# `sharpelab_nb.drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/sharpelab_nb/drivers/`, re-exported from the package:

```python
from sharpelab_nb.drivers import SRS_DC205, Yokogawa7651, ANC350
```

The `drivers` package (`src/drivers/`: `FastBi1K5`, `QSwitch`, `ContactMux`,
the VTI `SRS_DC205`, …) is documented separately in
[`drivers.md`](drivers.md).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (fixed-duration ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, *, ramp_num_points=100, ramp_wait_time=0.01, **kwargs)`.
Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint (7 dp) |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading over
  `ramp_num_points` steps spaced `ramp_wait_time` apart (so the duration is
  roughly fixed regardless of ΔV), **plus a mandatory 10 s settle when
  `|Δvolt| > 0.1 V`**. (The VTI `drivers.SRS_DC205` of the same name uses
  rate-based (`ramp_rate` V/s) semantics and has no fixed settle — they are not
  interchangeable.)

---

## `Yokogawa7651` — programmable DC source (pre-SCPI, write-only cached)

`Yokogawa7651(name, address, *, coil_constant=None, **kwargs)`. The 7651 is
pre-SCPI (no `*IDN?`) and cannot report programmed values back over the bus, so
**all set parameters are write-only with a software cache**.

| parameter | unit | R/W | range / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volt` | V | W | ±30 V |
| `current` | A | W | ±0.12 A |
| `field` | T | W | requires `coil_constant=`; range = ±0.12·|coil| |
| `mode` | — | W | `'VOLT'` (F1;) / `'CURR'` (F5;) |
| `output` | bool | W | output enable |

- After a kernel restart the cache is empty, so the ramp methods raise unless
  the cache is seeded first: **`set_voltage_cache(value)`** /
  **`set_current_cache(value)`**, or pass `start=` to the ramp call.
- **`ramp_voltage(target, step=0.01, delay=0.05, start=None)`** /
  **`ramp_current(target, step=0.001, delay=0.05, start=None)`** — software ramp
  from the cached (or `start=`) value; `step` must be `> 0`.
- When `coil_constant` is given, `field.step`/`field.inter_delay` are
  pre-configured for safe ramping (0.1 mT / 0.1 s ⇒ ~1 mT/s).
- `trigger()` sends `E;` (normally automatic after each set). `get_idn()`
  returns a static dict.

---

## `ANC350` — attocube piezo motion controller (rotator)

`ANC350(name, dll_dir, *, device_no=0, num_axes=3, **kwargs)`. Loads
`anc350v2.dll`/`libusb0.dll` from `dll_dir`; exposes `num_axes` axes as a
`ChannelTuple` at `.axes` (each an `ANC350Axis`).

### `ANC350Axis` (one stepper axis)
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | — | R | raw status int (decode via `is_moving`/`is_at_eot`/`has_sensor_error`/`is_sensor_disconnected`) |
| `position` | counts | R | raw sensor int32 (INT32_MAX when sensor power is off — the toploader default) |
| `rotation_count` | — | R | full-rotation counter |
| `amplitude` | mV | R/W | step drive amplitude, 0–70 000 |
| `frequency` | Hz | R/W | step frequency, 1–2000 |
| `dc_level` | mV | R/W | constant DC for fine positioning (output must be enabled) |
| `output_enabled` | bool | W | HV output; reads a software tri-state cache (True/False/None) — `set_output_cache()` to seed after restart |

Methods: `step(direction, count=1, *, wait=True, timeout=60.0, poll_interval=0.05)`
(±1 = forward/backward), `step_continuous(direction)`, `stop()`,
`wait_until_idle(…)`. `step`/`step_continuous` refuse to run unless the output
cache is `True`.

---

## Lock-in servo (`lockin_servo`)

Closed-loop positioning of an `ANC350Axis` against a lock-in voltage readback.
Not re-exported from the package — import from
`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.

### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.
=========== DRIVERS ===========
# `drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/drivers/`, imported package-qualified
(`from drivers.FastBi1K5 import FastBi1K5`). QCoDeS `Instrument` /
`VisaInstrument` subclasses plus two house helpers (`ContactMux`,
`bring_up_qdac_gate`). `measurement-env` is the source of truth for these.

The `sharpelab_nb.drivers` package (`SRS_DC205`, `Yokogawa7651`, `ANC350`,
lock-in servo) is documented separately in
[`sharpelab-nb-drivers.md`](sharpelab-nb-drivers.md).

---

## `FastBi1K5` — magnet supply (CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5)

`FastBi1K5(name, host, **kwargs)`. Raw TCP ASCII (port 10001). Out-of-plane
field in Tesla via the coil constant `T_per_A = 1/7.3`.

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | T | R/W | **get** = measured (averaged) current readback × `T_per_A`; **set** = blocking ramp (see below) |
| `is_ramping` | — | R | controller ramp flag (REG:STATUS bit 21) |

- **`field(target)` blocks**: issues the setpoint, polls `is_ramping` until
  clear, then a `settle_s` dwell (default 3 s). The set-point is **not**
  retrievable as a field — get always returns the measurement; never infer
  field from the last set call. Last commanded target is stashed at
  `commanded_field` (property).
- Non-blocking path: **`start_field_ramp(target)`** issues and returns
  immediately; pair with **`wait_for_ramp(timeout=None, tol=None)`** (poll the
  ramp flag, then settle — flat `settle_s` if `tol is None`, else poll the
  readback to within `tol` Tesla; `timeout=None` auto-bounds from `|ΔB|/slew`,
  `math.inf` waits forever). This enables measure-while-ramping.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: the ramp is commanded before the wait; a kernel
  interrupt leaves the supply ramping to its last target. Recovery is calling
  `field()`/`start_field_ramp()` again — there is no abort method.
- Limit: `max_field_T = 14.0`; targets beyond it (or beyond the `field`
  validator) raise before any setpoint is sent (checked on both the blocking
  and non-blocking paths).
- Switch / output: `heater_on()` / `heater_off()` (each blocks 10 s, no
  field-matching check), `output_enabled()`, `persistent_switch_on()` (reads);
  `status()` prints a summary. `start_field_ramp` raises if the persistent
  switch is off or the output is disabled.
- Tunables: `settle_s`, `poll_interval_s` (0.02), `slew_T_per_s` (= 1/7.3/60).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (rate-based ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, **kwargs)`. Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(final_volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading at a
  **constant rate**: `ramp_rate` V/s (attribute, default 5) over
  `ramp_num_points` (default 50) steps. Rate-based ⇒ deterministic dV/dt at any
  move size (gate-safe). (The toploader's `sharpelab_nb.drivers.SRS_DC205` is a
  different driver with fixed-duration ramp semantics — not interchangeable.)

---

## `Lakeshore_335` — temperature controller

`Lakeshore_335(name, address, **kwargs)`. Serial `VisaInstrument`.

| parameter | unit | R/W | command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_temperature` | K | R | `KRDG? A` |
| `vaporizer_temperature` | K | R | `KRDG? B` |
| `sample_setpoint` / `vaporizer_setpoint` | K | R/W | loop 1 / 2 setpoint |
| `sample_range` / `vaporizer_range` | — | R/W | heater range (int) |
| `sample_power` / `vaporizer_power` | % | R/W | manual heater output |

Methods: `set_sample_closed_loop()`, `set_vaporizer_closed_loop()`,
`off(heater='both'|'sample'|'vaporizer')`, `set_both(temperature, ratio=1)`

servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.
=========== DRIVERS ===========
# `drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/drivers/`, imported package-qualified
(`from drivers.FastBi1K5 import FastBi1K5`). QCoDeS `Instrument` /
`VisaInstrument` subclasses plus two house helpers (`ContactMux`,
`bring_up_qdac_gate`). `measurement-env` is the source of truth for these.

The `sharpelab_nb.drivers` package (`SRS_DC205`, `Yokogawa7651`, `ANC350`,
lock-in servo) is documented separately in
[`sharpelab-nb-drivers.md`](sharpelab-nb-drivers.md).

---

## `FastBi1K5` — magnet supply (CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5)

`FastBi1K5(name, host, **kwargs)`. Raw TCP ASCII (port 10001). Out-of-plane
field in Tesla via the coil constant `T_per_A = 1/7.3`.

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | T | R/W | **get** = measured (averaged) current readback × `T_per_A`; **set** = blocking ramp (see below) |
| `is_ramping` | — | R | controller ramp flag (REG:STATUS bit 21) |

- **`field(target)` blocks**: issues the setpoint, polls `is_ramping` until
  clear, then a `settle_s` dwell (default 3 s). The set-point is **not**
  retrievable as a field — get always returns the measurement; never infer
  field from the last set call. Last commanded target is stashed at
  `commanded_field` (property).
- Non-blocking path: **`start_field_ramp(target)`** issues and returns
  immediately; pair with **`wait_for_ramp(timeout=None, tol=None)`** (poll the
  ramp flag, then settle — flat `settle_s` if `tol is None`, else poll the
  readback to within `tol` Tesla; `timeout=None` auto-bounds from `|ΔB|/slew`,
  `math.inf` waits forever). This enables measure-while-ramping.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: the ramp is commanded before the wait; a kernel
  interrupt leaves the supply ramping to its last target. Recovery is calling
  `field()`/`start_field_ramp()` again — there is no abort method.
- Limit: `max_field_T = 14.0`; targets beyond it (or beyond the `field`
  validator) raise before any setpoint is sent (checked on both the blocking
  and non-blocking paths).
- Switch / output: `heater_on()` / `heater_off()` (each blocks 10 s, no
  field-matching check), `output_enabled()`, `persistent_switch_on()` (reads);
  `status()` prints a summary. `start_field_ramp` raises if the persistent
  switch is off or the output is disabled.
- Tunables: `settle_s`, `poll_interval_s` (0.02), `slew_T_per_s` (= 1/7.3/60).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (rate-based ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, **kwargs)`. Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(final_volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading at a
  **constant rate**: `ramp_rate` V/s (attribute, default 5) over
  `ramp_num_points` (default 50) steps. Rate-based ⇒ deterministic dV/dt at any
  move size (gate-safe). (The toploader's `sharpelab_nb.drivers.SRS_DC205` is a
  different driver with fixed-duration ramp semantics — not interchangeable.)

---

## `Lakeshore_335` — temperature controller

`Lakeshore_335(name, address, **kwargs)`. Serial `VisaInstrument`.

| parameter | unit | R/W | command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_temperature` | K | R | `KRDG? A` |
| `vaporizer_temperature` | K | R | `KRDG? B` |
| `sample_setpoint` / `vaporizer_setpoint` | K | R/W | loop 1 / 2 setpoint |
| `sample_range` / `vaporizer_range` | — | R/W | heater range (int) |
| `sample_power` / `vaporizer_power` | % | R/W | manual heater output |

Methods: `set_sample_closed_loop()`, `set_vaporizer_closed_loop()`,
`off(heater='both'|'sample'|'vaporizer')`, `set_both(temperature, ratio=1)`

"""Landau-fan design arithmetic: gate vectors along D=0, B grid, price."""
import numpy as np
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD
from hera.analysis import field_invB, GateCalibration, luttinger_frequency

CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
TG_MIN, TG_MAX = -0.3, 1.0
BG_MIN, BG_MAX = -1.3, 2.0

# --- accessible n along D = 0 within the TG limit (TG is the binding one)
for n in (-1.30, -1.27, -1.25, -1.20, 3.20, 3.25, 3.27, 3.30):
    vtg, vbg = calc_gate_voltages(n, 0.0, **CAL)
    ok = TG_MIN <= vtg <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= vbg <= BG_MAX
    print(f"n={n:+.2f}e12 -> Vtg={vtg:+.4f} Vbg={vbg:+.4f}  {'ok' if ok else 'OUT'}")

N_FAST = 85
n_vec = np.linspace(-1.25, 3.25, N_FAST)
Vtg = np.array([calc_gate_voltages(n, 0.0, **CAL)[0] for n in n_vec])
Vbg = np.array([calc_gate_voltages(n, 0.0, **CAL)[1] for n in n_vec])
print(f"\nn: {n_vec[0]:+.3f} .. {n_vec[-1]:+.3f} e12, step {n_vec[1]-n_vec[0]:.4f}e12, {N_FAST} pts")
print(f"Vtg: {Vtg.min():+.4f} .. {Vtg.max():+.4f} (span {Vtg.ptp():.4f} V); step {abs(Vtg[1]-Vtg[0])*1e3:.2f} mV")
print(f"Vbg: {Vbg.min():+.4f} .. {Vbg.max():+.4f} (span {Vbg.ptp():.4f} V); step {abs(Vbg[1]-Vbg[0])*1e3:.2f} mV")
print("within limits:", (Vtg.min() >= TG_MIN and Vtg.max() <= TG_MAX and Vbg.min() >= BG_MIN and Vbg.max() <= BG_MAX))

# --- B grid uniform in 1/B
for N in (100, 110, 120, 130):
    B = field_invB(1.0, 10.0, N)
    d = np.diff(1/B)
    print(f"N={N}: d(1/B)={abs(d).max():.5f} -> F_Nyq={1/(2*abs(d).max()):.1f} T; dF_res={1/(1/B.min()-1/B.max()):.2f} T; "
          f"dB max={abs(np.diff(B)).max():.3f} T")

N_B = 120
B_vec = field_invB(1.0, 10.0, N_B)
print(f"\nB: {B_vec[0]:.3f} .. {B_vec[-1]:.3f} T, {N_B} rows; dB: {abs(np.diff(B_vec)).min():.4f} .. {abs(np.diff(B_vec)).max():.3f} T")

# --- price (calibrated on run 5: 4158 pts / 4873 s = 1.172 s/pt at fast_delay=1.0)
SPT = 4873/4158
pts = N_B * N_FAST
t_pts = pts * SPT
t_ramp = (B_vec[-1]-B_vec[0]) / 0.137 * 60           # bare magnet ramp, s
flyback = (Vtg.ptp()/0.005)*6e-3                      # TG steps home at volt.step
SLOW_DELAY = 2.0
t_turn = N_B * (flyback + SLOW_DELAY + 3.0)           # + magnet settle_s 3 s
pre = 1.0/0.137*60
tot = t_pts + t_ramp + t_turn
print(f"\npoints {pts} x {SPT:.3f} s = {t_pts/3600:.2f} h")
print(f"magnet ramp (9 T @0.137 T/min) = {t_ramp/3600:.2f} h")
print(f"row turnaround {N_B} x ({flyback:.1f} flyback + {SLOW_DELAY} slow_delay + 3 settle) = {t_turn/3600:.2f} h")
print(f"pre-ramp 0->1 T = {pre/60:.1f} min")
print(f"TOTAL = {(tot+pre)/3600:.2f} h  (+8% realism -> {(tot+pre)*1.08/3600:.2f} h)")

N_FAST = 85

print(f"Vbg: {Vbg.min():+.4f} .. {Vbg.max():+.4f} (span {Vbg.ptp():.4f} V); step {abs(Vbg[1]-Vbg[0])*1e3:.2f} mV")

    print(f"B={B:4.1f} T: LL(nu-4) spacing dn={dn:.3f}e12 ({dn/(n_vec[1]-n_vec[0]):.1f} fast pts); "
          f"nu-1 spacing {dn/4:.3f}e12 ({dn/4/(n_vec[1]-n_vec[0]):.1f} pts)")

# vti-02 — session plan (stacking order of tetralayer graphene)

*Reconstructed and extended at the 2026-08-23 instance handoff. Steps 0–3 were
executed by the previous instance (runs 0–7); steps 4+ are mine. Kept current
as data lands.*

## Goal

ABAB (Bernal) vs ABCA (rhombohedral) vs ABCB (mixed) for vti-02, region-resolved
over the measured pair (only `sr1` = B_1 − B_2 is wired — one region), evidence-cited,
per the brief's output contract.

## Discriminators I am actually testing

| observable | ABAB (Bernal) | ABCA (rhombohedral) | ABCB (mixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| # of Fermi surfaces at D = 0 | **2** (two bilayer-like subbands, different band edges → the second turns on above a threshold \|n\|) | **1** (single quartic/flat band, 4-fold degenerate) | **2**, strongly unequal (trilayer-rhombohedral-like + monolayer-like) |
| SdH frequency content | two tones, ΣF_i = F_L(n); ratio **drifts with n** | one tone, F = F_L(n) exactly | two tones, very asymmetric, strong particle–hole asymmetry |
| F(n) at low \|n\| | one tone below the second band's threshold, kink where it turns on | single tone, linear through origin | asymmetric between e and h |
| CNP vs D | gaps weakly | gaps **strongly** (large R_CNP at \|D\| > 0) | intermediate / region-dependent |
| CNP at D = 0, B = 0 | semimetallic, low R | low-to-moderate | — |

**The sum rule ΣF_i = |n|·h/4e is the internal check** that also calibrates the
geometry prior (c_tg, c_bg are uncalibrated in absolute scale).

## Steps

- **0. Gate C — liveness.** `gate-current-sanity-check`, runs 0–3. Done: contacts
  alive, R(CNP, D≈0) ≤ 330 Ω, gate leakage in the tens of pA.
- **1. 0 T gatemap** → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`. Runs 4 (aborted, railed) and
  **5**. Done: CNP line slope c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), D_offset = −0.013 V/nm from
  the R_CNP(D) vertex, n_offset = −0.089×10¹². D = 0 line spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹².
  Side-observation: R_CNP rises from ≤ 330 Ω at D ≈ 0 to > 2.2 kΩ at D = +0.3 V/nm —
  a D-induced gap, qualitatively favouring rhombohedral character, **not decisive**.
- **2. Feasibility model.** Done (previous instance): F_L(3.2×10¹²) = 33.1 T;
  candidate ABAB split ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T.
- **3. SdH spot checks.** Runs **6** (e, n = +3.2×10¹², 0 → 10 T) and **7**
  (h, n = −1.2×10¹², 10 → 0.3 T). Done. Result: superb quality — R_xx minima reach
  ~0 Ω above 2 T, onset by ~0.3–0.7 T. **Ambiguous by construction**: run 6's FFT
  gives 7.5 / 15 / 22.5 / 30 T — an exactly commensurate ladder, so
  "single 30 T surface + harmonics/symmetry-breaking" (ABCA) and
  "7.5 + 22.5 = 30 T two-band" (ABAB) both fit one density. Run 7 gives 5.0 / 12.5 T
  — note 5.0 + ... does not obviously close on F_L = 12.4 T either.
  **→ one density cannot separate these. Frequencies must be tracked vs n.**
- **4. Landau fan at D = 0 — the discriminator. ← NEXT (this step)**
  B slow (1 → 10 T, uniform in 1/B, 130 rows), (V_tg, V_bg) co-swept fast along the
  calibrated D = 0 line, n = −1.25 … +3.25×10¹², 85 points. ~5 h 30 m.
  Establishes: F_i(n) for every tone on both carrier signs; the sum rule
  (→ absolute capacitance calibration); whether a second branch turns on at a
  threshold density (ABAB/ABCB) or one tone tracks F_L everywhere (ABCA); the
  Landau-level degeneracy sequence; the ν = 0 behaviour at the CNP.
  **What would change my mind mid-run:** a rail across many n columns (re-size
  sensitivity and restart), a leak trip, or no n-dependent LL structure by 3 T.
- **5. Low-field light-tone check (conditional, ~40 min riding 10 → 1 T).**
  Run 6's low-B leg was sampled at 50 mT (F_Nyq = 2.5 T at 0.5 T) — too coarse to
  test whether the ~7.5 T tone survives *below* the field where the 30 T tone dies.
  A tone that outlives its putative fundamental cannot be that fundamental's
  harmonic. Fine 1/B sampling 0.4 → 1.5 T at 2–3 densities settles it.
  Runs only if step 4 leaves the harmonic-vs-band question open.
- **6. D-dependence at fixed n (conditional).** How fast the tones split / the CNP
  gaps with D separates rhombohedral from Bernal. Cheap if it rides an existing field.
- **7. The call** — final cell of the ana notebook, per the output contract.
- **8. Close-out** — `return-to-initial` per the brief.

## Standing constraints

- τ(sr1) = 0.3 s at 24 dB/oct → 10τ = 3 s for a full settle; the session has been
  running gate fast axes at `fast_delay = 1.0` (3.3τ) since run 4. Kept for
  continuity with the run-5 calibration; the residual is a small, *constant*
  lag along the fast axis (same sweep direction every row), i.e. a shift in n,
  not a corruption. Flagged to the operator rather than changed unilaterally
  (front-panel-owned setting).
- Field is the expensive axis (0.137 T/min, blocking). Never re-traverse: the fan
  ends at 10 T so the conditional steps ride back down.
- Banned: gate-limit probing, standalone Si survey. Si stays at 0 V.

## HERA — Step 4: Landau fan at D = 0 (`landau-fan`) — the stacking discriminator

**Why this, now.** The spot checks are ambiguous *by construction*, and one density cannot fix them. Run 6 (n = +3.2×10¹², `data/6`) is superb data — R_xx minima reach ~0 Ω above 2 T, oscillations from below 1 T — but its FFT over 2–10 T returns **30.0 / 22.5 / 15.0 / 7.5 T**, an exactly commensurate ladder. Two readings fit it equally well: (a) **ABCA** — one 4-fold-degenerate Fermi surface at F = 30 T carrying the whole density (F_L(3.2×10¹²) = 33.1 T from the geometry prior, 9 % high, i.e. within the uncalibrated capacitance scale), with the lower tones as harmonic/symmetry-breaking structure of a strongly non-sinusoidal oscillation; (b) **ABAB** — two bilayer-like subbands at **7.5 + 22.5 = 30 T**, closing the sum rule ΣF_i = |n|h/4e, with 15 T the 2nd harmonic of the light tone and 30 T the breakdown/sum orbit. Run 7 (n = −1.2×10¹², `data/7`) gives 5.0 / 12.5 T against F_L = 12.4 T — same knot. `sdh_onset` on run 6 separates them only suggestively: the ~7.1 T tone is still above threshold at the record's 0.3 T edge while the 22.2 / 29.5 T tones onset at 1.33 / 1.91 T.

**The discriminator is F(n), not F.** Harmonics keep an exactly integer ratio at *every* density; two real subbands do not — their ratio drifts with n because the bands have different DOS, and in Bernal tetralayer the second subband has a different band edge, so below a threshold |n| only one tone exists and a **kink** appears where the second turns on. ABCA gives one tone tracking F_L linearly through the origin on both carrier signs; ABCB gives two strongly unequal tones with marked particle–hole asymmetry. This fan measures F_i(n) on both signs in one run, and the sum rule doubles as the absolute calibration of c_tg/c_bg (run 5 fixed only their *ratio*, 0.773; the scale is still the 9.5/11 nm geometry prior).

**Design choices.** Field is the expensive axis (0.137 T/min, blocking) so it is the *slow* one, traversed once, monotonically up from where the magnet sits — 65.7 min of pure ramp inside the run, never re-traversed. The 130 rows are spaced **uniform in 1/B** (`field_invB`) so `sdh_fft` gets an already-even record: F_Nyquist = 71.7 T (above the ~60 T second harmonic of the highest tone, so nothing can alias down onto a candidate band frequency — this is what sets the row count), frequency resolution δF = 1.11 T. B_lo = 1.0 T, not lower: extending to 0.5 T at this Nyquist would cost 266 rows. The fast axis is (V_tg, V_bg) **co-swept along the calibrated D = 0 line** through the CNP, n = −1.25 … +3.25×10¹² — the full width the TG operating limit allows (it binds at −1.27 / +3.27, and the cell asserts both gate vectors inside the committed validators before anything moves). 85 points ⇒ 0.054×10¹² step, which resolves the ν-spacing-1 ladder above ~5 T and the ν = 4k ladder above ~2 T.

**Coverage trade, stated.** Below 1.0 T the fan sees nothing — so the "does the light tone outlive the heavy one" test (a tone cannot be a harmonic of a fundamental it survives below) is **not** settled here. Run 6's own low-field leg can't settle it either: it was sampled at 50 mT, i.e. F_Nyquist = 2.5 T at 0.5 T, far too coarse for a 7.5 T tone. That test is plan step 5 — fine 1/B sampling 0.4 → 1.5 T at 2–3 densities, ~40 min, riding the magnet back down from the 10 T this run ends at. Buying it inside *this* fan instead would roughly double the run. Also not covered: any D ≠ 0 (plan step 6) and any temperature dependence (LK masses are hard here anyway at T_e ≈ 8 K).

**Preconditions the cell prints before it commits** (it asserts, then stops on mismatch): T_sample 1.0–1.5 K with a live logfile, |B| < 0.05 T (the magnet is at +0.003 T after the handoff close-out), V_si = 0, gates at 0 V, Keithley nplci = 1/1, persistent switch on and output enabled. Sensitivity is fixed at **200 µV = 20 kΩ full scale** for the whole fan — 38× run 6's maximum (530 Ω), sized per the run-4 lesson to the map's largest feature rather than the 1D peak. The one thing that may still clip is the CNP column itself at high field (the ν = 0 state, |n| ≲ 0.1×10¹², ~3 of 85 columns); a clip there is a reportable lower bound on the ν = 0 gap, not a loss of the fan. Gate leakage trips the run at 1 nA (run-7 flyback transients ran ~200 pA, 5× margin).

**Checkpoints** (`hera-watch data --next --follow`, armed with this cell): **first rows at B ≈ 1 T** — signal level, railing across the row, leakage, the R(n) trace reproducing the run-5 gatemap's D = 0 cut; abort there if the channel rails broadly or the CNP peak is misplaced. Then at **~2 T**, **~4 T** and **~7 T**: per-column FFT on the landed rows — is LL structure developing in n, are two tones separating, is the sum rule closing. Abandon if no n-dependent LL structure has appeared by 3 T. The run ends with the gates parked at 0 V and the **field left at 10 T on purpose**, so plan steps 5/6 ride it down instead of paying 66 min each way.

carrying the version tag and an appended_at UTC timestamp) so they can be
filtered and timed later. Re-running with the same args double-inserts.

positional arguments:
  notebook              Path to .ipynb (absolute or relative to cwd).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --markdown TEXT       Append a markdown cell with this source. Pass '-' to
                        read the cell from stdin; multiple '-' flags consume
                        successive chunks separated by a line of '---|'.
                        Repeatable; order preserved across all
                        --markdown/--code variants.
  --code TEXT           Append an un-executed code cell with this source. Pass
                        '-' to read the cell from stdin (see --markdown for
                        chunk semantics). Repeatable; order preserved across
                        all --markdown/--code variants.
  --markdown-file PATH  Append a markdown cell whose source is read from PATH
                        (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --code-file PATH      Append an un-executed code cell whose source is read
                        from PATH (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --summary TEXT        One-line dense spec of the proposed measurement.
                        Rendered into the FIRST appended markdown cell, right
                        after its leading heading (or prepended if the cell
                        has none) as a timestamped blockquote: '> **14:32** ·
                        <summary>' — the clock is server-local time at append;
                        _/* in the text are escaped for rendering. Also
                        stamped verbatim to metadata.hera.summary on that
                        cell. Requires at least one markdown cell among the
                        appended cells (--markdown/--markdown-file); must not
                        contain a backtick. At most once.
  --eta DURATION        Expected runtime for the proposed measurement — '40m',
                        '2h', or '1h30m' (optional <N>h then optional <N>m, h
                        before m; at least one required, total > 0; fractional
                        values rejected). A bare number like '40' is REJECTED
                        — add the m/h suffix. Rendered into the FIRST appended
                        markdown cell's blockquote line (with --summary or
                        alone) as '**ETA ~15:12** (≈40 min)' in server-local
                        time, computed from the same append instant; crossing
                        local midnight adds ' (+1d)' right after the clock.
                        Also stamped as an ISO-8601 UTC instant to
                        metadata.hera.eta_at on that cell, and echoed to
                        stdout as 'eta: ~15:12 (≈40 min)'. Requires at least
                        one markdown cell among the appended cells. At most
                        once.
  --execute             After appending, run the last appended code cell
                        YOURSELF by the id this append just created (never
                        nb['cells'][-1] off the stale on-disk file). Policy-
                        gated like execute-cell (append_exec or edit_exec),
                        checked before any cell lands. Exit code reflects the
                        cell's status. Mutually exclusive with --wait.
